meta.concept:
Neon Fugitive is a fully 3D open-world cyberpunk bounty-hunter game for PC built on Unity 6000.0 LTS with the Universal Render Pipeline (URP). The core player mechanics involve third-person movement combining foot parkour—wall-running, vaulting, and sliding—with rideable hoverbike driving in open sections. Input handling is managed via the Input System package to support both on-foot agility and vehicle control, while Cinemachine handles camera perspective using a lock-on targeting mode that locks onto high-priority marks during chases. The project architecture requires distinct Unity scenes for each of the six districts plus the main menu, boss arena, and credits to isolate lighting conditions and audio contexts specific to zones such as the rain-soaked industrial docks or corporate towers.

Key technical systems must include a vehicle controller for hoverbikes, a health and damage manager handling shields and healing pickups, and a bounty system capable of tracking multiple live contracts simultaneously. Enemy AI utilizes NavMesh agents with distinct states for patrol, chase, and alert zones within the district map. Procedural geometry tools are required to generate terrain for the outer slum district, road network grids for markets, water planes for flooded zones, and room layouts for tower interiors using ProBuilder level generation at edit time or runtime. A Dialogue Manager will play in-world hologram events corresponding to story beats, while a District Manager switches ambient audio tracks like the industrial drone or chase adrenaline music per zone transition.

Visual fidelity relies on URP post-processing with essential bloom and chromatic aberration effects applied to achieve the stylized neon-on-dark aesthetic defined by the NeonFugitive color palette. A Day-night cycle controller must drive scene lighting and NPC schedules across all eight narrative acts, synchronized with a Minimap radar displaying bounty targets and district boundaries. The audio system requires an audio manager to layer eight distinct tracks ranging from looping rain thunder environments to non-looping combat SFX packs and victory stings, ensuring action punctuation does not break immersion. Finally, a save and checkpoint system must persist state between acts to maintain narrative progression through the escalating story beats defined in the activation sequence.
meta.user_prompt:
Neon Fugitive — a third-person open-world cyberpunk bounty-hunter game for PC.

The player is a rogue AI enforcement agent navigating six districts of a rain-soaked
megacity at night. Each district has its own visual identity: neon markets, industrial
docks, corporate towers, underground tunnels, a rooftop skyway, and the flooded
outer slums. All six districts plus a main menu, a boss arena, and a credits scene
must be separate Unity scenes.

NARRATIVE — eight acts of escalating story beats:
1. Activation: player boots up for the first time in an alley (on_start)
2. First Mark: player receives the first bounty contract (on_enter_zone)
3. Street Chase: player pursues mark through market crowds (on_enemy_death)
4. Betrayal: handler reveals the player is also a target (on_timer)
5. Underground: player escapes into the tunnel district (on_enter_zone)
6. Data Heist: player steals identity files from corporate tower (on_pickup)
7. Showdown: final confrontation with the original programmer (manual)
8. Escape: player reaches the sky-bridge extraction point (on_enter_zone)

AUDIO — rich layered soundscape across eight tracks:
- Pulsing synth main theme (looping music, plays on menu)
- District market ambient (looping ambient, tense urban crowd)
- Industrial dock drone (looping ambient, machinery hum and water)
- Chase adrenaline track (looping music, fast-paced synth percussion)
- Corporate tower tension (looping music, slow arpeggiated suspense)
- Rain and thunder environment (looping ambient, outdoor weather)
- Combat hit and gunshot SFX pack (non-looping sfx, action punctuation)
- Victory sting and credits outro (non-looping music, emotional resolution)

PROCEDURAL GEOMETRY — runtime-built world pieces:
- Procedural terrain for the outer slum district (terrain type, resolution 64)
- Procedural road network grid for market district (road type, resolution 48)
- Procedural water plane for the flooded outer zone (water type, resolution 32)
- Procedural room layout for the corporate tower interior (room type, resolution 24)

SYSTEMS — everything this game needs:
- Third-person player movement with parkour (wall-run, vault, slide)
- Cinemachine third-person camera with lock-on targeting mode
- Enemy AI with NavMesh patrol, chase, and alert states
- Bounty system tracking multiple live contracts simultaneously
- Health and damage system with shields and healing pickups
- Dialogue manager playing all eight story beats as in-world hologram events
- District manager switching ambient audio and sky color per zone transition
- Day-night cycle controller driving scene lighting and NPC schedules
- Vehicle controller for rideable hoverbikes in open sections
- Weapon system managing ranged and melee attack combos
- Inventory and equipment screen
- Minimap radar displaying bounty targets and district boundaries
- Save and checkpoint system between acts
- ProBuilder level generator producing the tunnel and rooftop districts at edit time

VISUAL STYLE: stylized — heavy neon on deep dark backgrounds.
COLOR PALETTE name "NeonFugitive":
  primary   #00F5FF  (player energy — cyan glow)
  secondary #1A0A2E  (environment base — near-black violet)
  accent    #FF2D78  (enemies and hazards — hot pink)
  background #0D0D1A (sky and voids — pitch dark blue)
  trim      #FFD600  (UI, collectibles, highlights — electric yellow)

RENDER PIPELINE: URP (post-processing bloom and chromatic aberration essential).
UNITY VERSION: 6000.0
PLATFORM: PC

audio_cues.gen_prompt: Heavy metallic raindrops striking wet concrete surfaces with distant thunder rumbling overhead.
High-pitched electric whine from magnetic repulsion coils vibrating through the chassis frame.
Synthetic soles scraping against slick metal walls while magnetic clamps engage and disengage.
Soft blue static crackling as a translucent data stream projects from a wrist-mounted emitter.
Rapid mechanical servos whirring inside enemy exoskeletons as they pivot toward the target.
Deep subterranean dripping sounds echoing off submerged concrete pillars and rusted pipes.
High-frequency digital chirps rising in pitch as energy barriers fracture under kinetic impact.
Low hum of magnetic elevators shifting floors while distant glass doors slide open silently.
Sharp crystalline chimes resolving into a warm analog synth bassline for mission completion.
Loose gravel crunching underfoot mixed with the distant drip of leaking industrial pipes.
